title: Types of denominators and general forms
intro: Read this before any partial fraction question. The form you choose decides everything.

blocks.title: proper or improper
blocks.body: A fraction $\dfrac{P(x)}{Q(x)}$ is **proper** when $\deg P<\deg Q$. If it is not proper, divide first (long division), then decompose the remainder fraction.

blocks.title: finding the constants
blocks.body: Multiply both sides by the denominator, then either **substitute** the roots (cover-up) or **compare coefficients**. A good check: substitute $x=0$ at the end.

blocks.title: the slips
items: A repeated factor needs **one term for each power**: $(x-1)^2$ gives two terms.
An irreducible quadratic gets a **linear** numerator $Bx+C$, not just a constant.
A constant can turn out to be $0$. That is allowed.

blocks.title: typed answers
blocks.body: Write a fraction constant as `4/3`. For several constants, the blanks are filled in the order $A$, $B$, $C$.
